'''Talitha Washington''' (born 1974) is an American mathematician and academic who specializes in applied mathematics and [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]] education policy.<ref name="gifted">[http://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/talitha-m-washington/ Black History Month 2018 Honoree: Talitha M. Washington] mathematicallygiftedandblack.com</ref> She was recognized by [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] as a [[Black History Month]] 2018 Honoree.<ref name="gifted" /> Washington became the 26th president of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] in 2023.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="awmpres" />

==Education and career==
Washington was born in [[Frankfort, Indiana]], and adopted at a young age by Ruthanne and [[Walter Wangerin Jr.|Walter Wangerin]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Rev. Walter Martin Wangerin Jr. Obituary (1944 - 2021) The Times|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/nwitimes/name/walter-wangerin-obituary?id=22628631|access-date=2021-11-05|website=Legacy.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Talitha Washington - Biography|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Washington/|access-date=2021-11-05|website=Maths History|language=en}}</ref> She was raised in [[Evansville, Indiana]], and attended [[Benjamin Bosse High School]].<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://acenotes.evansville.edu/view.cfm?issueId=167 | title = Talitha Washington at Howard University until Fall 2012 | website = AceNotes Today | date = May 17, 2011 | publisher = [[University of Evansville]] | access-date = October 28, 2019}}</ref> After serving in [[Costa Rica]] with the [[AFS Intercultural Programs|American Field Service]], she earned a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics from [[Spelman College]] in 1996.<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor|id=Washington}}</ref> She then attended the [[University of Connecticut]], earning a master's degree in 1998 and a [[Ph.D.]] in 2001. Her doctoral thesis was ''Mathematical Model of Proteins Acting as On/Off Switches,'' under the supervision of Yung-Sze Choi.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|89003}}</ref>

Washington served on the faculty of [[Duke University]] from 2001 to 2003, the [[College of New Rochelle]] from 2003 to 2005, the [[University of Evansville]] from 2005 to 2011, and [[Howard University]], starting in 2011, where she became associate professor of mathematics.<ref name=gifted/> After a few years on leave as a program director at the [[National Science Foundation]],<ref name=nsf>{{cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/staff/staff_bio.jsp?lan=twashing&org=NSF&from_org=NSF|title=Talitha M. Washington {{pipe}} NSF - National Science Foundation|website=nsf.gov|accessdate=2019-01-26}}</ref> in 2020 she became the inaugural director of the [[Atlanta University Center Consortium]] (AUCC) Data Science Initiative. In 2022 she became president-elect of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] and assumed the presidency on February 1, 2023.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.pr.com/press-release/854220|title=Talitha Washington Elected President of the Association for Women in Mathematics|website=www.pr.com|access-date=January 7, 2023}}</ref><ref name="awmpres" /> In 2025, Washington was named the executive director of the Howard University Center for Applied Data Science and Analytics and the Sean McCleese Endowed Chair in Computer Science, Race, and Social Justice.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Brittany |first1=Bailer |title=Talitha Washington Named Executive Director of Howard University Center for Applied Data Science and Analytics |url=https://thedig.howard.edu/all-stories/talitha-washington-named-executive-director-howard-university-center-applied-data-science-and |website=The Dig |publisher=Howard University |access-date=10 March 2026}}</ref>

Washington's research interests include [[Nonstandard finite difference scheme|nonstandard finite difference]] (NSFD) schemes for certain systems of differential equations, including [[population model]]s, [[one-dimensional]] systems, and the [[Black–Scholes equation]].<ref name=gifted/><ref>''[https://www.math.ksu.edu/research/lectures/posters/chatelain/Washington.pdf Finite Difference Schemes that Achieve Dynamical Consistency for Population Models]'' Thirteenth Virginia L. Chatelain Memorial Lecture presented by Talitha Washington at Kansas State University on November 9, 2017</ref>

==Education policy and awards==
Washington is active in education policy, especially best practices on achieving racial and ethnic diversity in STEM.<ref name=NSFDUE>[https://coas.howard.edu/content/mathematics-professor-talitha-washington-receives-prestigious-nsf-due-appointment Mathematics Professor Talitha Washington Receives Prestigious NSF DUE Appointment]  Howard University, College of Arts and Sciences</ref> At the NSF, she has served as co-lead of the Hispanic-Serving Institutions Program and is a graduate of the STEM diversity organization [[SACNAS]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=HHMI Advanced Leadership Institute Alumni - SACNAS |url=https://www.sacnas.org/leadership-programs/ali-cohorts |access-date=2023-09-30 |website=www.sacnas.org |language=en}}</ref> She serves on the Council of the [[American Mathematical Society]] and served on the Executive Committee of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] (AWM).<ref name=usbe>''[http://www.blackengineer.com/news/hidden-no-dr-talitha-washington/ Hidden no more: Dr. Talitha Washington]'' by Lango Deen, US Black Engineer Information Technology Magazine, January 9, 2018</ref>

Washington helped to champion the once-forgotten mathematician [[Elbert Frank Cox]] (1895–1969)  from her hometown of [[Evansville, Indiana|Evansville]],<ref name=gifted/> leading to the November 2006 unveiling of a plaque honoring the longtime Howard professor as the first [[African-American]] scholar to earn a doctorate in mathematics.<ref>[http://www.ams.org/notices/200805/tx080500588p.pdf Evansville Honors the First Black Ph.D. in Mathematics and His Family] by Talitha M. Washington</ref> She received the 2019 Black Engineer of the Year Awards STEM Innovator Award.<ref>''[http://www.blackengineer.com/article/howard-university-professor-receives-innovation-award/ Howard University Professor receives Innovation Award]'' US Black Engineer Information Technology Magazine, January 31, 2019</ref>

Talitha Washington was named a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]], Class of 2021. Her citation read "For contributions to broadening the participation of underrepresented groups, and service to the mathematical profession".<ref name="AMSfellow">{{cite web |title=Class of 2021 Fellows |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi |publisher=American Mathematical Society |accessdate=2 November 2020}}</ref>  Washington was also named a Fellow of the AWM, Class of 2021, "for her dedication to raise awareness of African American women in STEM; for her lifelong promotion of Historically Black Colleges and Universities; and for her unwavering dedication to the [[National Association of Mathematicians]]."<ref name=awmfellow>{{cite web |title=The AWM Fellows Program: 2021 Class of AWM Fellows |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2021-awm-fellows/ |publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics |accessdate=7 December 2020}}</ref> On February 1, 2022, she became president-elect of the AWM.<ref name="awmpres">{{Cite web|last=Taylor|first=Tommy Jr.|title=Talitha Washington Elected President of the Association for Women in Mathematics {{!}} The AUC Data Science|url=https://datascience.aucenter.edu/awm_presidentelect_talithawashingon/|access-date=2022-02-06|language=en-US}}</ref> She was elected to the 2022 class of Fellows of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 AAAS Fellows {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) |url=https://www.aaas.org/page/2022-fellows-0 |access-date=2023-03-15 |website=www.aaas.org |language=en}}</ref>
